checklist.notes: The repair dialogue, distinction between TTS and listening-capable checks, success condition, and unavailable-check fallback are explicit; only the setup for obtaining a hidden TTS order remains underspecified.
Four timed stages, one minimal-pair contrast, and a four-line final exchange are appropriately bounded for 35 minutes at A1.1.
Articulation, repair language, separate listening and speaking checks, and role-play now form a consistent practice-to-verification sequence.
The personal-fact exchange, misunderstanding repair, turn-taking, and independent intelligibility check directly support basic participation.
The lesson progresses from controlled vowel production through modeled repair and modality-specific checking to a short integrated exchange.

The v4 blocker is resolved: TTS is explicitly limited to playback, while speaking verification now requires an independent listener or a suitable speech-recognition tool and permits “not checked” when unavailable.
Concrete tongue-position and vowel-length guidance can support relevant perception and production work without asserting a universal Vietnamese-learner deficit.

findings.description: The listening step asks a self-study learner to play a “hidden order” in TTS and later reveal it but does not state who or what prepares and conceals that order.
findings.recommendation: When next revised, name a simple independent randomization or helper workflow so the learner cannot see the sequence before listening.
